name: European Cybersecurity Competence Centre
evidence_rating: thin: output counts and audit findings only; headline 25% market-share target not tracked; no independent study
summary: The Centre in Bucharest channels EU cybersecurity funding with Member States. The infrastructure it oversees (26 CyberHubs, 27 national centres) is in place, but the Centre only became operationally independent in late 2024, auditors found gaps in its reporting, and its headline aim of a 25% global market share for EU cybersecurity firms by 2027 is not being tracked.

indicators.indicator: Number of cybersecurity infrastructure/tools jointly procured
indicators.evidence: 26 cybersecurity infrastructures (CyberHubs, incl. two cross-border) procured and first 12 tools deployed under Digital Europe, in line with targets.

indicators.indicator: Global market share of European cybersecurity suppliers
indicators.evidence: No data on market share found in Commission or ECCC reporting.

indicators.indicator: Patents, publications, commercial products from next-generation cybersecurity technologies
National coordination centres; people trained; curricula aligned
indicators.evidence: Network of 27 national coordination centres set up; stakeholders cite standardised practices and cross-border cooperation as main benefits. ECCC reached financial autonomy only in September 2024.

indicators.indicator: Independent Commission evaluation of the Centre

literature.citation: European Commission (2018), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal establishing the European Cybersecurity Industrial, Technology and Research Competence Centre and the Network of National Coordination Centres (executive summary SWD(2018) 404), SWD(2018) 403
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal establishing the European Cybersecurity Industrial, Technology and Research Competence Centre and the Network of National Coordination Centres (executive summary SWD(2018) 404)
literature.outcomes: industrial competitiveness; market share; R&D uptake
literature.headline: Fragmented EU cybersecurity market dominated by non-EU firms; preferred option (Competence Centre plus network, Art. 173/187 TFEU) expected to help EU industry raise market share; target 25% global market share by 2027
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected a new competence centre pooling EU and national money to strengthen Europe's cybersecurity industry, aiming for a 25% global market share by 2027.

literature.citation: European Commission (2025), The Digital Europe Programme: Main findings of the interim evaluation (cybersecurity objective), COM(2025) 771 (SWD(2025) 420)
literature.title: The Digital Europe Programme: Main findings of the interim evaluation (cybersecurity objective)
literature.method: interim evaluation of the funding programme the ECCC implements
literature.headline: 26 CyberHubs procured in line with targets; 27 national coordination centres; first 12 cybersecurity tools deployed with first users in health
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's review of Digital Europe reports that the cybersecurity infrastructure the Centre oversees has been bought on schedule, but says nothing yet about effects on Europe's cybersecurity industry.

literature.citation: European Court of Auditors (2025), Annual report on EU joint undertakings for the 2024 financial year, ECA annual report
literature.title: Annual report on EU joint undertakings for the 2024 financial year
literature.headline: ECCC achieved financial autonomy only on 24 Sept 2024; did not disclose members' cumulative contributions or compare them with targets; internal control framework only partly implemented
literature.summary_plain: EU auditors found the Centre became independent from the Commission only in 2024 and cannot yet show how much Member States have contributed.
